title: Track 1 safety and audit recovery-stream isolation

catch_all_membership_before.measured_from: the production job-type map, not the brief
catch_all_membership_before.note: the classifier kept them clear of the legacy prefixes since it was written, but distinguishable is not the same as typed

journal_lane.behaviour: grouped every catch-all job into ONE stream, so anything completing closed anything that failed
reproduced_before_fix: a failed Track1 STOP_REPAIR closed by a Track1 AUDIT
a failed Track1 AUDIT closed by a Track1 STOP_REPAIR

journal_lane.seen_in_production: Stage 5ZZT measured TRACK1_STOP_REPAIR_1820 closing two failed SPY refreshes on 2026-08-27

issue_lane.behaviour: fell back to the job id when the type was `other`, so each sweep stood alone
issue_lane.consequence: a Track 1 sweep that failed at 06:20 could NEVER be closed by the identical sweep at 08:20, while its legacy counterpart always could
issue_lane.found_by: reading the second reader; this half was not in the brief

both_max_hold_spellings: the slot table declares track1_maxhold_exit; the log label reaching the reader is TRACK1_MAX_HOLD_EXIT. Matching one would type the job on some days and not others.
matching_is_structured: on the type, never a substring - TRACK1_STOP_REPAIR_0620 contains STOP_REPAIR, and a substring test would merge the two routes' sweeps, which is the one thing B1 exists to keep apart

isolation_after.design_note: every must-not-close has a must-close beside it; a change that stopped closing anything would satisfy half the suite and be worse than the bug it replaced. Mutation M8 exists to make that unshippable.

wording_changed.before: the `other` branch said 'the job emitted an unclassified error' and advised reconciling current broker state - for jobs that never touch the broker

after.track1_safety_stop_repair: protective stops on the Track 1 book were not rechecked at this slot
after.track1_safety_stop_repair_recovered: the Track 1 book was rechecked when <job> completed; no immediate action
after.track1_safety_max_hold: a position past its maximum hold would not have been closed
after.track1_window_audit: no evidence record was written for that window; nothing is at risk in the book, and the paper-evidence gate reads that record

wording_changed.pinned: a test asserts the word broker appears in none of the audit impact or action text, in either failure state

ui.attribution_fixed: these jobs reached the scheduler-owned list THROUGH `other`; typing them without naming them explicitly would have moved a missed sweep to `runner` - blamed on a runner that never ran
ui.labels: the job id moved to the tooltip; the row shows a readable name such as 'Track 1 stop-repair sweep 06:20'
ui.label_scope: the three types this stage introduces ONLY
ui.why_scoped: the first attempt covered strategy slots and legacy sweeps: it broke five Stage 5ZE tests that address a row by its id and a sixth that finds a row by looking for STOP_REPAIR in its name. Renaming a taxonomy is a design change of its own.
ui.test_updated: one Stage 5ZE test now reads the id from the tooltip, which is where this stage put it
ui.unknown_type_fallback: renders the job id, never blank (mutation M14)

my_own_error_caught_by_the_suite.what: the label helper was inserted next to stripScheduleBad, three scopes deep inside a render function, so jobLabel was invisible at the journal row

my_own_error_caught_by_the_suite.precedent: the same mistake as Stage 5ZZL, where render calls landed inside a click handler
my_own_error_caught_by_the_suite.fix: moved beside mvEsc at module scope, and the patch asserts the destination brace depth is 1 rather than trusting indentation

b1_reopened_during_this_stage.operator_action: rerun the account baseline check to close B1 again; nothing is at risk while it stands open
